title: The multiplication of the constant group scheme: the components of T_E x_T T_E and the glued morphism
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $E$ an abelian group. Let $T_E=\coprod_{e\in E}T$ be a coproduct of copies of $T$ indexed by $E$, with coprojections $\iota_e:T\to T_E$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], let $\pi:T_E\to T$ be the morphism with $\pi\circ\iota_e=\mathrm{id}_T$ for all $e\in E$, and $V_e=\iota_e(T)\subseteq T_E$. Let $P=T_E\times_{\pi,T,\pi}T_E$ be the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $p,q:P\to T_E$, put $\rho=\pi\circ p=\pi\circ q:P\to T$, and $W_{e,e'}=p^{-1}(V_e)\cap q^{-1}(V_{e'})\subseteq P$ for $(e,e')\in E\times E$. Then: (a) the $W_{e,e'}$ are open and closed subsets of $P$, $W_{e,e'}\cap W_{d,d'}=\varnothing$ for $(e,e')\ne(d,d')$, and $P=\bigcup_{(e,e')\in E\times E}W_{e,e'}$; (b) regarding each $W_{e,e'}$ as an open subscheme of $P$ [def-weil-open-immersion], there is a unique morphism of schemes $m:P\to T_E$ with $m|_{W_{e,e'}}=\iota_{e+e'}\circ\rho|_{W_{e,e'}}$ for all $(e,e')\in E\times E$; (c) $\pi\circ m=\rho$, $m(W_{e,e'})\subseteq V_{e+e'}$ for all $(e,e')$, and consequently $m^{-1}(V_d)=\bigcup_{e+e'=d}W_{e,e'}$ for every $d\in E$.

source.place: Groupoids, Example 39.5.6 (Tag 03YW, label example-constant-group): 'The morphism giving the group structure is the morphism $G\times G\to G$ which maps the component corresponding to the pair $(g,g')$ to the component corresponding to $gg'$' (over $\Spec\mathbf Z$, then base changed to $S$); that the pairs index a decomposition of the fibre product into open and closed pieces and that the componentwise maps glue to one morphism is not written out in Stacks, so the proof is to be written by an agent (gluing: Schemes Section 26.14, Tag 01JA)

proof.text: Use Mathlib sigmaOpenCover to cover the coproduct. The point equality criterion sigmaι_eq_iff makes different component images disjoint. Each component is open by IsOpenImmersion.isOpen_range; its complement is the union of all other component images, so it is closed. Preimages along the continuous pullback projections give clopen pair components. Two different pairs differ in a coordinate, so disjointness of the corresponding coproduct components proves disjointness of the pair components. Choose an index for each projection of a point using sigmaOpenCover.exists_eq to prove that the pair components cover.

source.place: Groupoids, Example 39.5.6 (Tag 03YW, example-constant-group): 'the component corresponding to the pair (g,g')' of $G\times G$; the decomposition of the fibre product into these components is not written out there and is written here

proof.text: Let C be Scheme.Pullback.openCoverOfLeftRight of the two sigmaOpenCover covers. Mathlib Scheme.Pullback.range_map, with base map the identity of T, identifies Set.range (C.f ij) with the pair component W_ij. Define the local map f_ij as C.f ij followed by the square projection and the inclusion indexed by ij.1 + ij.2. For equal indices, pullback.condition proves compatibility. For different indices the ranges are disjoint, so Scheme.isEmpty_pullback makes the overlap empty and isInitialOfIsEmpty.hom_ext proves compatibility.

proof.text: Use C.hom_ext and the restriction formula to prove m followed by the codiagonal equals the square projection; Sigma.ι_desc makes each inclusion followed by the codiagonal the identity. Given a point of W_ij, the range formula provides a preimage under C.f ij. Evaluate the restriction formula at that point to exhibit its image under m as lying in the component indexed by the sum.

source.place: Groupoids, Example 39.5.6 (Tag 03YW): the multiplication 'maps the component corresponding to the pair (g,g') to the component corresponding to gg''; with Schemes, Lemma 26.14.1 (Tag 01JB) for the uniqueness of glued morphisms

proof.text: For the inverse image formula, a point of the preimage of V_d lies in some W_ij by the pair cover. Its image lies in V_(ij.1+ij.2) by the preceding step. Disjointness of the coproduct components forces ij.1+ij.2=d. This supplies the required subtype index of the union. Conversely evaluate the MapsTo property at any pair with sum d.
